headline: NEW FOUND GOLD DOUBLES QUEENSWAY NPV TO C$1.73B IN REVISED PEA — 1.5Moz Project Economics Surge at $4,000 Gold
snippet: New Found Gold nearly doubled the projected value of its Queensway gold project in Newfoundland to C$1.73 billion ($1.23B US) in a revised preliminary economic assessment, as the updated study applies current $4,000+ gold prices in place of the original $2,500 base case. The project — centred on the Appleton Fault Zone in central Newfoundland — had already demonstrated a 56.3% IRR and 1.5Moz mine plan in its July 2025 PEA, and the revised economics underscore how gold's sustained run above $4,000 has structurally transformed the NPV math for high-grade Tier-1 projects that were already economic at half today's price.

headline: CHINA LEADS GLOBAL GOLD RUSH — PBOC Adds 21 Tonnes in Sept, 23rd Straight Month; 45% of Central Banks Plan More Buying
snippet: China's central bank purchased approximately 21 tonnes of gold in September — its 23rd consecutive month of buying and its largest single-month addition in three years — pushing PBOC gold reserves to 2,196 tonnes. The World Gold Council reports total announced central bank gold purchases of 170 tonnes through August 2026, with 45% of central banks surveyed planning further purchases within the next year. The sustained institutional accumulation stands in notable contrast to the retail-driven softness seen in gold and gold equity prices ahead of the October 28 FOMC meeting.

headline: LIBERTY GOLD HITS 52-WEEK HIGH ON BLACK PINE RC RESULTS — 1.78 g/t Au over 47.2m, Three Holes Above 1.4 g/t in Idaho
snippet: Liberty Gold's stock hit a 52-week high following new RC drill results from its 2026 program at Black Pine in Idaho, highlighted by 1.78 g/t gold over 47.2 metres, 1.51 g/t over 48.8 metres, and 1.45 g/t over 45.7 metres — with six of ten reported holes returning grades above 1.12 g/t. The consistent, broad oxide gold mineralization at shallow depths supports the economics of a conventional heap-leach operation and positions Black Pine among the more compelling advanced-stage oxide gold projects in the western United States.

headline: NEWMONT RED CHRIS CAPITAL HITS $4.2–4.8B REAL — 15Mtpa Block Cave, FID Pending, Commercial Production 2033
snippet: Newmont disclosed in its Q3 2026 earnings release that the underground block cave expansion at Red Chris in British Columbia will require $4.2–4.8 billion in real-term development capital — net of a C$500 million federal infrastructure contribution — with commercial production targeted for 2033. The figure is nearly double the 2021 prefeasibility estimate, reflecting updated engineering, inflation, and a decision to raise processing capacity to 15 million tonnes per year, making Red Chris the largest new copper-gold development project in Canada and a key datapoint for understanding true greenfield copper capex inflation in this cycle.

headline: GOLDMAN: CHINA'S REAL GOLD ACCUMULATION 2X+ OFFICIAL PBOC FIGURES — Sovereign Off-Books Flow May Top 25T/Month
snippet: Goldman Sachs research published October 19 estimates that China was the largest identifiable gold buyer in August at approximately 25 tonnes, but flags that actual Chinese sovereign accumulation is likely running two to three times the disclosed PBOC figures — with the excess flowing through state-owned enterprises and sovereign wealth vehicles rather than direct central bank balance sheets. If Goldman's estimates prove accurate, the structural price floor embedded in gold's demand model is substantially higher than mainstream buy-side consensus currently assumes.

headline: EUROPEAN LITHIUM SECURITYHOLDERS APPROVE CRITICAL METALS MERGER — Court Hearing Oct 26, Close Set for Nov 5
snippet: European Lithium securityholders approved the merger with Critical Metals Corp. at a vote held October 22, clearing the final shareholder hurdle for the deal. The final court approval hearing is scheduled for October 26, with scheme implementation — transferring European Lithium's assets including the Wolfsberg lithium project in Austria — expected by November 5. The deal consolidates one of Europe's few near-development lithium projects under a listed North American entity as Western governments race to build domestic critical mineral supply chains.

headline: ROYAL GOLD Q3 PRELIMINARY: $318M STREAM SALES, $49M BUYBACK, $250M DEBT REPAID — Full Results Due Soon
snippet: Royal Gold issued preliminary Q3 2026 estimates showing stream segment sales of $318.3 million at 74,700 GEOs with cost of sales of $834 per GEO, while simultaneously repaying $250 million of debt (leaving $150M drawn on its $1.4B revolver) and buying back 190,045 shares for $49 million. For junior mining investors tracking the royalty and streaming model, Royal Gold's quarter demonstrates the capital-return capacity that structured precious metals agreements generate when gold sustains above $4,000 — with minimal exposure to mine-level cost inflation.

headline: GRUPO MEXICO TO EXPAND RAY AND SILVER BELL COPPER MINES IN ARIZONA — Asarco Capex Unchanged Despite Q3 Output Dip
snippet: Grupo Mexico confirmed it will press ahead with major expansion projects at its Asarco operations in Arizona — including capacity upgrades at the Ray and Silver Bell open-pit copper mines — despite reporting a decline in Q3 copper output. The decision signals that Mexico's largest miner views the structural copper deficit thesis as durable enough to justify sustained US-based capex even as near-term LME prices pull back from September's record near $14,875 per tonne, and underscores why Arizona's copper belt continues to attract long-cycle investment commitments from major producers.

headline: MINERAL RESOURCES Q1 FY27 LITHIUM HITS RECORD 170,000 dmt SC6 — Bald Hill Restart Tracking FY27 Guidance
snippet: Mineral Resources delivered a record attributable 170,000 dry metric tonnes of SC6-equivalent lithium in Q1 FY27 (July–September 2026), keeping the company on track for its upgraded full-year guidance of 660,000–750,000 dmt SC6, supported by the Bald Hill restart approaching nameplate capacity of 140,000 t/yr. The result comes as Chinese lithium carbonate futures sit near 10-month lows — MinRes is delivering record volumes into a depressed price environment, though low-cost Wodgina and Bald Hill operations underpin economics well below current spot.

headline: FORRESTANIA LOCKS IN ZENITH MINERALS AT 58.99% — Takeover Offer Unconditional, Closes Nov 12
snippet: Forrestania Resources declared its ASX takeover offer for Zenith Minerals unconditional after accumulating a 58.99% relevant interest in Zenith's shares, crossing the compulsory acquisition threshold. The offer remains open until 5:00pm AWST on November 12, 2026, with withdrawal rights available for an additional two weeks for dissenting shareholders. The deal adds to a growing list of junior consolidation transactions on the ASX and TSX-V as elevated gold and copper prices make it economically rational to aggregate fragmented exploration tenements into development-scale packages.

headline: CME: ONE COPPER PRICE 'ISN'T EFFECTIVE ANYMORE' — Fragmented Pricing Creates New Risk for Junior Developers
snippet: CME Group's metals division head told Reuters that the era of a single global copper benchmark is ending, with LME and COMEX now trading at structurally different levels depending on trade policy and tariff regimes. For junior copper developers — where COMEX pricing often sets the project economics baseline — the fragmentation means feasibility studies and NPV calculations need to stress-test against regional price scenarios rather than a single global quote, particularly as COMEX recently reversed the tariff-fear premium it held over LME earlier this year.

headline: RECORD CENTRAL BANK BUYING ISN'T SAVING MINING STOCKS — GDXJ Falls 2-5x Harder Than Spot Gold in 2026
snippet: A Discovery Alert analysis argues that despite central banks purchasing gold at near-record rates in 2026 — with China alone buying 170+ tonnes — junior and mid-tier gold equities are declining two to five times harder than spot gold itself, driven by rate expectations, equity risk-off sentiment, and cost inflation compressing mining margins even at $4,000 gold. The disconnect between bullion's fundamental drivers and equity market sentiment historically resolves in favour of miners — but the timing of that re-rating remains the key variable for junior mining investors.
